You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

For a grid with exactly two colors, map the more frequent color to the less frequent color, and map the less frequent color to 0, preserving positions and dimensions. Verified demos: 5-heavy with rare 6 → 5→6 and 6→0; 5-heavy with rare 4 → 5→4 and 4→0. Test confirmed 5→7 and 7→0. Do not assume fixed color identities; count each grid's frequencies. ## Task pattern: uniform straight separators recolored
A demonstrated ARC transformation: identify complete uniform horizontal/vertical lines (including multi-cell-thick bands) that act as separators, and recolor those separator cells to 2 while leaving all other cells unchanged. In the observed demo, the input had a top row entirely color 4 and two adjacent full-height columns entirely color 4; output changed those row/column separator cells to 2. In its test, the separators were a full-height column of 0 and full-width rows of 0, and replacing precisely those cells with 2 solved the puzzle. Treat the geometry of complete straight separator bands as the invariant; the line color can vary.

## Task pattern: fill enclosed rectangle
For task-2c92d428, a single closed rectangular outline with dangling line extensions was filled in its interior with color 4; preserve the boundary, outside extensions, and rest of grid. Demo confirmed the fill color; test was accepted. Details and coordinates in `memory/continual-arc-task-2c92d428.md`. Infer fill color from demonstrations for other tasks.
